clue.text: Flexible tempo and spirit shortened, as is conductor's stick

indicators.note: shortened means the spirit's word loses its final letter

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: as is says the conductor's stick is cut short in the same way as the spirit

parts.note: a conductor beats time with a baton

explanation.surface: A musician muses on loose tempo, a sawn-off baton and a drop of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts RUM to RU, and 'as is' cuts BATON the same way, to BATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is the musical term for expressive freedom of tempo, pulling the beat slightly back and forth.

clue.text: Prince appears more wet?

definitions.meaning: The Prince of Monaco who married Grace Kelly
the comparative of rainy, wetter in weather

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a royal looks soggier than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Rainier of Monaco shares his name with the comparative of rainy, meaning wetter.

clue.text: 16 down 9's dense mist rising among endless tiny individual individuals

indicators.note: among means the misty piece goes inside the shortened word
endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tiny is a little one, a baby

indicators.note: rising, in a down light, means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: fog is a dense mist
individual individuals are single ones, ones

explanation.surface: A thick fog creeps up among a crowd of small people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims BABY to BAB; 'rising' turns FOG into GOF, which goes 'among' BAB: BA(GOF)B, then ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bag of Bones is a 1998 novel by Stephen King, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Rising fat about to beat disease

indicators.note: about means the turned fat wraps round the beating word
rising, in a down light, means the word for fat reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Someone decides to pound some rising fat to cure an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns SUET into TEUS, which goes 'about' TAN: TE(TAN)US.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, or lockjaw, is a bacterial disease causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: Several 25s with same problem, covered in kisses

indicators.note: covered in means the rearranged word sits inside the kisses

parts.note: X is a kiss, so kisses are XS

indicators.note: problem suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Several festive seasons share the same trouble, all smothered in kisses.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 across is the word for Christmas, so 'several 25s' asks for its plural. 'problem' gives MASE, and 'covered in' wraps the kisses round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel means Christmas, and Xmas is the abbreviated form, so several of them are Xmases.

clue.text: 16 down 9's shocking story time (loveless Bates' heart repeatedly ignored)

indicators.note: shocking means the letters are thrown into disorder
ignored says the named letters are left out of the shuffled pool

parts.note: love is O, zero in tennis, and less says it goes

indicators.note: repeatedly means the middle letter is removed twice over
heart means the middle letter of the name

explanation.surface: A gruesome tale features Norman Bates of Psycho, in a story without love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' with 'ignored': the letters of STORY TIME, less O (love, the 'loveless') and T twice (Bates' heart, 'repeatedly'), rearrange to give the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is Stephen King's 1987 novel about a writer held captive by a fan.

clue.text: 16 down 9's moles cooked in seasoning

indicators.note: in means the rearranged animals go inside the seasoning

parts.note: salt is a seasoning

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A recipe for moles cooked with plenty of seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns MOLES into EMSLO, which goes 'in' SALT: SAL(EMSLO)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem's Lot is Stephen King's 1975 vampire novel.

clue.text: All about bird showing support for chest

indicators.note: about means the total goes round the bird

parts.note: the sum is all of it, the total
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Everything around a bird shows support for its chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All' looks like part of the surface's subject; it is the total. 'about' wraps that total round the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the ribcage that holds it together.

clue.text: 16 down 9's seen upside down, swallowing heads of dinosaurs, frogs, unicorns and larvae on weird night

indicators.note: swallowing means the turned word takes the rest inside it
upside down, in a down light, means the word is read from the bottom, backwards
on, in a down light, puts one piece above the next
heads of means the first letter of each creature
weird means the letters are put in strange order

explanation.surface: A nightmarish scene of dinosaurs, frogs, unicorns and larvae seen topsy-turvy on a weird night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' gives NEES and 'weird' gives THING; 'on' stacks the creatures' initials above it, and 'swallowing' puts both inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful Things is Stephen King's 1991 novel about a sinister shop in Castle Rock.

clue.text: See 16 down
On reflection they should see the paper? Cobblers!

parts.note: taken as written
MS is short for manuscript, a paper
in the fairy tale of the shoemaker, elves secretly make the shoes overnight

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that they ought to read the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers!' looks like British slang for nonsense; here it is the elves of the fairy tale who make shoes. The definition is the reflexive form of 'they', as in 'they hurt themselves'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, the reflexive pronoun corresponding to they is the form used when the action turns back on the subject.

clue.text: Indian meal made a difference at home

parts.note: a tiff is a minor difference of opinion, a squabble
in means at home

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out at home over an Indian dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a light midday meal or lunch in India, from Anglo-Indian usage.

clue.text: Walked over to small hill missing nothing in European city

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: trod means walked

indicators.note: missing means the zero is taken out of the hill

parts.note: a mound is a small hill
nothing is O, zero

explanation.surface: A hiker walks across to a little hill and finds nothing there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TROD into DORT; 'missing' takes O out of MOUND to give MUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Dortmund is a large industrial city in western Germany, famous for its football club.

clue.text: A dancing bear a Russian leader dismissed from square dancing position

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move about
dismissed from means those letters are removed from the word
leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A performing bear is ordered off a square by a Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns BEAR into RABE; 'dismissed from' removes A and R (a Russian leader) from SQUARE to leave SQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a ballet position on one leg with the other extended behind.

clue.text: Oddly, being a pickpocket is a fair attraction

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: a dipper is slang for a pickpocket

explanation.surface: Someone notes that it's strange to be a thief at a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' gives BIG from the odd letters of BEING.
explanation.definitionFit: The big dipper is a roller coaster ride at a funfair, a classic fairground attraction.

clue.text: Criticise sporting achievement

definitions.meaning: a grand ... is winning all the major tournaments in a season

explanation.surface: Someone is knocking an athlete's success.
explanation.definitionFit: Slam is both to attack verbally and, as in grand slam, a sweep of major sporting titles.

clue.text: Having run out of fuel, reverted to pudding

indicators.note: reverted means turned back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: O stands for out, as on a switch
gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone whose car ran dry went back to dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of fuel' gives O and GAS, and 'reverted' turns OGAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy grain from palm pith, made into a milk pudding in Britain.

clue.text: 'It' was one of his favourites, written up for sort of party piece

indicators.note: written up, in a down light, means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets
a hen party is a bride's night out before her wedding
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a favourite pet, written up as a party piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns PETS into STEP. It is Stephen King's horror novel about a killer clown.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a 1986 horror novel written by this author, so 'It' was one of his books.

clue.text: Events with theistical application I avoided

indicators.note: application suggests the letters being applied anew, so they are rearranged
avoided says this letter is left out of the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: Religious events are planned, with a person skipping the application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' with 'avoided': THEISTICAL less I rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics is the collective name for track and field events.

clue.text: One benefiting from Arsenal header embraced by supporters

indicators.note: embraced by means the letter sits inside the supporting words

parts.note: a leg supports a table
a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: header means the first letter, at the top of a down light

explanation.surface: An Arsenal player heads the ball and is hugged by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' does double duty as two different props, one for a table and one for a golf ball; 'embraced by' sets Arsenal's 'header' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a legacy under a will, so one who benefits from it.

clue.text: Fire-breathing monster takes tea, entertaining emir eccentrically

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the rearranged word inside

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: eccentrically means the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A dragon takes tea while hosting a strange Arab ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentrically' gives IMER, and 'entertaining' has the tea word host it, splitting after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Chimera was a fire-breathing beast with a lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail.

clue.text: 16 down 9's not quite made it to the other side?

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.words: made it to the other side
parts.note: carried means conveyed across, taken to the far side

explanation.surface: Someone almost reached the far side, or perhaps the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims CARRIED to its first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrie is Stephen King's 1974 debut novel about a telekinetic schoolgirl.

clue.text: Style of Japanese cooking fit ultimately for Tibetan bovine, eaten by ER II

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word
eaten by means the animal goes inside the royal title

parts.note: ER II is Elizabeth Regina the Second, the late Queen
the yak is a Himalayan ox

explanation.surface: The Queen dines on a Himalayan ox in a Japanese style.
explanation.walkthrough: ER II is the late Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher. 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'fit', and 'eaten by' tucks the Tibetan ox inside her title.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese method of grilling food glazed in a sweet soy marinade.

clue.text: Almost lose sight of what could be grotesque

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to go blind is to lose sight

explanation.surface: Someone nearly loses their vision staring at something hideous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims GO BLIND to GOBLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is an ugly mischievous creature of folklore, a typical grotesque figure.

clue.text: See 2
Craftsman of craft whips kinky Tory

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A boat builder whips a Conservative in a kinky scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' turns WHIPS into SHIPW.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwright builds and repairs ships, which are craft that sail.

clue.text: Present time for heartless book

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: A gift for Christmas: a book without much feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes V, the middle letter, from NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the season for presents, and Noel is another word for Christmas.

clue.text: Number about to enter river, getting cold feet

indicators.note: to enter means the letter goes into the turned number
about means the number is turned round

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A swimmer about to wade into a river gets cold feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' wants to be N; it is SEVEN, turned by 'about' to NEVES, with R put in by 'to enter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves means anxiety or apprehension, the same jitters as having cold feet.

clue.text: Girl sought by man who may be showing his age?

indicators.note: may be showing hints the letters could appear in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is pursued by an older man revealing his years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be showing' rearranges HIS AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese girl or woman trained to entertain as a hostess.
